source_relation: Historical Bishal Paija subcontract clauses are conceptual precedents only. Do not copy confidential parties, prices, brand specs, penalties, subcontract restrictions or old time periods.

clause_families.rule: Written included works and exclusions control commercial obligations. Distinguish general structural/services works from specific finishing/compound works.
Signed Appendix A drawing register governs technical details only. Require number, revision, date, attachments and signature before treating drawings as contract documents.
Changes in scope, materials, drawings, price or programme require both parties' prior written approval. Structural deviations may require qualified engineer review.
Workmanship and materials require specifications and approved substitutions; differentiate owner-supplied materials and contractor-supplied materials.
Financial schedule must reconcile against contract value. Written event certification required for commencement and completion milestones; due days are a project-specific approved term.
Specify final withheld instalment versus proportionate deductions, start event, calendar duration and release prerequisites. No invented deductions.
DLP appears separately from last payment trigger; DLP duration does not itself delay the retained final instalment unless expressly agreed.
Demolition and material title transfer must be clearly stated; confirm lawful authority, third-party rights, permitted recovery, safety and waste disposal.
Provide written notice, fair cure opportunity, negotiation and legally reviewed dispute routes; never copy historical penalties or interest rates by default.
Do not issue an agreement before party authority, taxes, dates, signed appendices, payment terms and legal review are resolved.

For every original drawing set linked to a contract, record canonical provider ID, MIME, exact source digest, total pages and numbered-sheet citation ranges. Separate what the source actually depicts from commercial user scope and any engineering signoff.

Default A/B/C arrangement keeps original drawings separate: Document A cites Document B by exact file, revision and sheet/page; Document C separately governs candidate/approved materials. Only append original PDFs verbatim upon explicit request and preserve unmerged originals. Attachment or citation never implies signed design approval.

For unprovided plumbing/electrical routes and compound/railing design, say mutual written contractor-client agreement is required; an available septic/soak-pit detail does not prove complete plumbing design. Changes to railing grade/scope must have independent VO controls.

Use clear client-facing document names with version and no internal DRAFT/AUDIT marker. Render an ordinary agreement title, legal effectiveness/signature conditions, and human-readable references; never print internal lifecycle status, machine IDs, QA, AI/implementation terms or source digests in the contract. Separately maintain full unsigned/execution status, internal QA and evidence in restricted Drive/private manifests. This respects docs/document-engineering/enterprise-client-visible-semantics-v1.1.md.
Reconcile milestone slab/roof-level names and structural elements to signed sheet references before labeling structurally approved; drawings as-received are descriptive evidence only.

public_private.public: template control and safe formatting only
public_private.private: parties, project clause choices, approved rates, drawings, signatures

project_specific_copy_rule: Historic project-specific contracts may suggest clause questions but cannot be reissued as another client's signed terms. All new project deliverables require their own source and commercial agreement.

default_document_package.name: Architectural/Structural Drawing Register and Original Files

window_material_rule.rule: Use the project approved window material, not historical aluminium defaults. When user selects uPVC, define approved manufacturer/system, profile and glass subject to project-specific source and approval; historical 88 mm section and 5 mm glass are candidates, not universal normative requirements.
